page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU configuration. Built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked up to 3.7 GHz, this instance allocates 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores across 4 hardware threads. The underlying CPU is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Hardware support includes AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent.

A primary architectural characteristic of this instance is its high memory density relative to processing cores. The instance features 128.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an allocation of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 644 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space alongside support for premium remote storage. Accelerator hardware is not included, with GPU count standing at zero. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are also omitted.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, as reflected by a stress-ng single-core score of 2702.68 placing in the top quartile. However, because overall CPU resources are constrained to 4 vCPUs, multi-core throughput scores in the lower quartile across tests such as multi-core stress-ng (5400.57), Geekbench multi-core (3669.0), and PassMark CPU (6185.74). Memory subsystem testing reveals uncached large-block read speeds of 39.9 GB/sec alongside large-block write throughput of 22.94 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 4.17 million operations per second, while static web serving achieves 5.07 GB/sec.

The constrained core topology offers qualitative cost efficiency for environments governed by per-core database software licensing where substantial memory capacity is mandatory. While parallel throughput is bounded by the four available vCPUs, the large memory allocation and bundled local solid-state storage provide an appropriate profile for in-memory caches, memory-bound database engines, and medium-scale analytics tasks that do not saturate high core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance engineered around a constrained vCPU footprint. Running on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture at speeds up to 3.7 GHz, the virtual machine provides 4 vCPUs spanning 2 dedicated physical cores and 32 MB of L3 cache. It pairs these compute resources with an expansive 128.0 GB of memory, yielding 32.0 GB per vCPU, and incorporates a 644 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage without integrated GPU hardware. Synthetic testing reflects strong single-thread compute capabilities, though overall multi-threaded throughput is strictly limited by the low core allocation. Memory bandwidth reaches 39.9 GB/sec on large read blocks. This setup delivers targeted resource efficiency for workloads requiring extensive memory footprints alongside minimal core-based licensing, such as specialized database systems, Redis instances, and memory-intensive enterprise software.
